sections.description:
NORTH WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE LOCAL COUNCILS NAMING AND RENAMING OF
PUBLIC PLACES RULES, 1994
NORTH WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE
LOCAL COUNCILS NAMING AND RENAMING OF PUBLIC PLACES RULES, 1994
[Gazette of N.‑W.F.P.
Extraordinary, Part I, 13th March, 1996]
No.AOV/LCB/1‑44/85, dated
10‑8‑1994.‑‑‑In exercise of the powers conferred
by section 172 of the North‑West Frontier Province Local Government
Ordinance, 1979 read with sections 82 M(64) 83‑A thereof the Government
of North‑West‑Frontier Province is pleased to make the following
rules namely:‑‑
1. Short title and
commencement.‑‑(1) These rules may be called the North‑West
Frontier Province Local Councils Naming and Renaming of Public Places Rules,
1994.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. A Council may, with the
prior approval of Government, assign a name to a road, street, square, park or
any other public place or change the name of any such road, street, square,
park or any other public place:
Provided that no such name shall
be assigned or changed, unless the proposal of naming or re‑naming, as
the case may be, has been published in press for inviting objections and
suggestions of public in such manner as a Local Council may determine.
3. A road, a street, a
square, a park or any other public place shall named after a person, Pakistani
or foreign, if he/she‑‑
(i) is a historical personality.
(ii) has rendered distinguished
services to the cause of humanity, nation, the Province of N.‑W.F.P. or
local area: or,
(iii) has been either a
President, Prime Minister, Governor, Chief Minister, a President of a political
party or political leader with distinct services to the nation or the Province
of N.‑W.F.P.;
(iv) is/was a renowned scholar, a
scientist of repute, an eminent artist, a war hero, an outstanding sportsman or
a public servant or of eminence;
(v) a philantheopist, a social
worker who has recognized services at the international, national or provincial
level.
4. No road, street,
square, park or other public place shall be named after a person if he/she is a
sitting member of the local council, the Provincial Assembly or the National Assembly,
or he holds any office under the Government, a Local Council or a public
authority.
5. A name once assigned
under these rules shall not be changed unless a period of at least fifty years
has lapsed.
